rationale: A uses the well-known closed-form method. It sorts the counts, derives the natural group sizes from the differences between neighbouring counts, then turns as many (5,3) pairs as possible into (4,4). Each step is short and has a comment, and it is clearly correct, since the 5+3 to 4+4 swap is the only improving exchange. B is a greedy loop driven by a custom rule (counts[2] > counts[3]) that is harder to check by reasoning. It repeats the decrement blocks in every switch case and re-sorts on each pass. Its doc comment also presents 4+2 against 3+3 as a trade-off when 4+2 is plainly cheaper, which suggests the reasoning behind the rule is muddled. B's named price constants are nice, but A is simpler, more obviously correct and more efficient.
